6542106:
Tallavont School

The Tallavont School was founded centuries ago by idealists seeking to foster a sense of community in Eastgate by creating an institution that would allow teachers persecuted in their home countries for their political beliefs to teach here instead of being entangled in the city's treacherous and infighting politics. Called "the Fortress" because it incorporates an old war keep from the city's early history, this structure defines the district's skyline and is visible for miles around.⁠ Teachers often use the height to give lessons from the balconies, offering views of the city and providing their students with a unique teaching perspective. A quarter of the students live in Eastgate, while the rest come from noble families in the city or abroad who send their children to study here.⁠
9887516:
Shrine of Saint Senex

The Shrine of Saint Senex is not dedicated to a deity but instead to the centuries-dead Senex, an oracle who devoted her life to recovering the drowned dead of Nisroch Bay and the Yolubilis River. The shrine is now all but forgotten by the modern world; Saint Senex fell in popularity after the Chelaxian Civil War, lying unremembered on a stretch of swampy coast on Argo Isle, just south of the city of Kintargo. The driftwood shrine is devoted to drowned sailors,⁠ including a buried sanctum that is home to the bodies of dozens of unknown drowned.⁠ The shrine is shielded from magical divination and has sometimes been used as a secret safe house by Hellknights of the Order of the Torrent. Thanks to its decline in prominence, the shrine's only inhabitants are now a pair of rag-clad oracles.⁠
12214296:
Caverns of Pirthous

The Caverns of Pirthous are a maze of caves and tunnels beneath Iobaria's Syrzemyan Highlands. The caverns are the secret winter homes and refuge of the Azorva centaur clans; no humanoid has ever discovered their entrances and returned to tell of them.⁠
20309016:
Aysepir's Astounded Abyss

Aysepir's Astounded Abyss is a carnival show of unusual, and often disturbing, beings in the Puddles district of Absalom. Despite having the trappings of fiction and making extraordinary claims, its employees are exactly what they are presented to be—beings of sometimes immense power afflicted by curses or misfortune, or simply being of unique parentage.⁠⁠
22991566:
Auginford

Auginford is a small village in southern Nidal near the southern Usk River.⁠
26801296:
Fort Drejas

Fort Drejas is one of the many forts abandoned by Nirmathas during the war with Molthune. The fort is located in the southern area, right where the Marideth River flows into Lake Encarthan. Easy access to the river is one of the fortification's strategic advantages.⁠
29001216:
Sunhill Monastery

Sunhill Monastery is located on a plateau just west of the Zho Mountains of Qadira. The complex contains chapels to both the empyreal lord Ragathiel and the goddess Sarenrae. It is the headquarters of the Eleli who are overseen by a peri named Nuryah.⁠
29978926:
Temple of Asmodeus

The Temple of Asmodeus stands out in an anarchic city like Kaer Maga, but its faith predates that of Cheliax, and since religious freedom is important in the city, this gothic temple has gained its own renown. It is located directly opposite the Bank of Abadar, symbolizing an alliance between the two clergy, and although it offers similar services to the temple across the way, those seeking infernal pacts can find them here.⁠
40330926:
Nirodin Villa

Nirodin Villa is a stately townhouse in the northwest of Magnimar's Alabaster District. Situated directly next to Kaddren Villa, it is the seat of House Nirodin,⁠ and run by Cheiskaia Nirodin, the family's matriarch.⁠
58443996:
Sanctum of the Sorrowmaker

Sanctum of the Sorrowmaker is a labyrinthine cavern complex in Dahak's Fang island that Aashaq the Annihilator and her minions call home.⁠
66250796:
Anactoria

Anactoria is a settlement in the rural inland of the Ustalavic county of Caliphas on the banks of the Droa River and south of the Albria Woods.⁠⁠

The village is famous across Ustalav for the Maid of Anactoria, a corpse that was found in the local bogs in an incredibly well-preserved state despite its great age, which is now displayed in one of the village's cottages. The locals make their living cutting peat, which is exported across Ustalav as a cheap fuel.⁠
67172856:
Mount of Black Fire

The Mount of Black Fire is an extraordinary mountain in the Tusk Mountains. Unlike other active volcanoes, this mountain spews forth a dark ebony flame. Even more strangely, this ebony fire puts out regular fire. This unstable fire comes from overlapping gates connected to the Plane of Fire and the Void inside the mountain.⁠⁠

Of particular interest is the attraction of the Blackfire Adepts, a group of powerful individuals associated with an arcane cult. The Blackfire Adepts are drawn to the Mount of Black Fire due to its connection to distant planes and the eldritch energies it possesses. However, despite their efforts, they have not yet discovered a means to fully master or control this unique and enigmatic power source.⁠
76485596:
Hangman's Harbor

Hangman's Harbor is a village along the Sellen River in Taldor, north of Cassomir. The village is located between the Sellen and a large granite cliff, and it covers not only the riverfront but the top of the cliff, and the cliff itself. Some of its buildings jut out over the water, some are wedged onto narrow ledges, and some are carved directly into the cliff face. Because of the lack of flat land, the village is very built up, with individual buildings often being shared by multiple businesses. The mayor's house boasts an ominous noose that prominently hangs over the river. The town is home to a tavern called The Hanging Bottle.⁠
77985656:
Willowside

Willowside is an old, reclusive town on the northwestern coast of the Isle of Kortos, which has suffered greatly from a strange phenomenon known as the Welt in recent years.⁠
86555306:
Bloomwreath

Bloomwreath is a town situated in western Kyonin⁠ around a greenhouse called the Great Blossom. Botanists recognize the plant species preserved in the greenhouse as species lost during Earthfall.⁠

The village's activities revolve around botany, from growing flowers to cutting topiary. The process is overseen by the founder, known as the High Gardener, who considers it her mission to preserve plants from around the world.⁠
90517436:
Hisuikarasu

Hisuikarasu (pronounced hee-soo-ee-Kah-rah-soo)⁠ is the capital of the tengu nation of Kwanlai, in Tian Xia. A relatively prosperous city in chaotic Kwanlai, Hisuikarasu is ruled by the half-celestial benevolent autocrat Lady Sutarai-Gongen.⁠ Lady Sutarai-Gongen's popularity is such that her power is beginning to spread beyond the capital to the rest of Kwanlai.⁠
100409776:
Founder's Archive and Museum of Ages

The Founder's Archive and the Museum of Ages are cultural and historical institutions that share a joint campus in the Capital District of the Varisian city of Magnimar.⁠ In Varisia, the museum is rivaled only by the Jeggare Museum in Korvosa.⁠ The library complex hosts a famous Forbidden Collection under lock and key, to which Madam Irba Demerios controls access.⁠
103908356:
Railford

Railford is a small settlement located on a small wooded hill a few miles inland from the larger settlement of Golsifar, on the Inner Sea coast of Taldor. The settlement is in the prefecture of Moda.⁠
104200716:
Gembasket

The Gembasket spans an area in the Barrier Wall mountains approximately a mile in diameter, across razored peaks, unexpected drops, rocky ground, and impassable rises. Natural resources are abundant within the Gembasket, including nodes of gemstones, precious metals, and veins of minerals that run its rocky walls. A narrow and dangerous path navigable only by experienced travelers winds up through the mountains to the Gembasket.⁠
107275876:
Heslandaena

Heslandaena is a subterranean settlement below the island of Dahak's Tooth in the Shackles. The cenotes that dot the island offer aquatic entry to miles of sea caves, which eventually emerge into unflooded, humid caverns. These moldy dark caves and passages lead to Heslandaena. The isolated town is inhabited by drow cut off from the Darklands many years ago by a curse.

The dark elves were part of the Harkule clan. They offended a powerful matriarch and were banished for their insolence. The isolated drow town is ruled by matriarch Pelanquelle, wicked and resentful for her exile. A number of pirate captains know about the drow settlement and are trusted by its ruler: Adis Vraisdottir, captain of the fast sloop North Wind, which sails out of Mezdrubal; White Hollis Dobilo, captain of the brig Stormrunner, which sails from Drenchport; and Constanza Purgote, captain of the sloop Constanza's Whim which sails from Port Peril.

The three pirates, each unaware of the others, all have lucrative trading deals with matriarch Pelanquelle bringing foodstuffs and supplies in exchange for raw gemstones and rare subterranean substances.⁠
134066416:
The Doomsayers' Stand

The Doomsayers' Stand is a stone dais amidst the maze of tents in the Lower City, once used by musicians to entertain. Starting in 4707 AR, various preachers of strange cults and faiths began using it to attract new followers to their mysterious dogmas, and the resulting clashes between these faiths have forced the Zephyr Guard to post guards around it at all times.⁠
135748976:
Bos-Phargrumm

Bos-Phargrumm is an ice castle perched high among the peaks of the Tusk Mountains northwest of the Ginji Mesa. It is the castle of Jarl Gnargorak, the self-proclaimed king of all frost giants.⁠⁠

The fortress is constantly built on top of the decaying older layers underneath, with the jarl and his most favored minions living in the newest, highest layers. Deep in the lower collapsed levels, many dangerous creatures make their home.⁠
153675056:
Talamir

Talamir, now known as Dragonscar, was a wealthy city whose prideful citizens once painted many of its buildings green and blue to match the flag of Taldor. It is now an ash-encrusted ruin charred by both volcanic and draconic flame.⁠⁠

177363216:
No-Horn

The No-Horn is a low quality tavern in Magnimar's Dockway neighbourhood. It typifies the sort of establishment that pops up periodically near the Bazaar of Sails, only to close again in short order. It is named for its sign, which depicts a hornless unicorn being tormented by drunken devils.

The structure itself is a rickety and leaning thing constructed from an old ship's hull. The establishment's barkeep is an ornery man missing both of his ears. Patrons can expect cheap food and drink here, but both are of an extraordinarily low quality.⁠
177403106:
Baallalota

Baallalota, the Swamp's Heart, is located in the heart of the Graidmere Swamp north-east of Lake Prophyria, near the far north-eastern border of the Ustalavic county of Sinaria.⁠ Baallalota is an area of ground within the Graidmere where daughters of the swamp dance a ritual on the night of the vernal equinox to determine the year's Queen of Baallalota.⁠
182440336:
Xin-Shalast

The fabled city of Xin-Shalast was once the capital of the Thassilonian realm of greed, Shalast, under the reign of Runelord Karzoug. Located far from civilization in the heart of the Kodar Mountains, Xin-Shalast's existence was considered mythical until it was recently rediscovered,⁠⁠ and the restored Runelord Sorshen selected it as the capital of her revived New Thassilonian nation of Eurythnia in 4718 AR.⁠⁠
210324776:
The Kiln

The Kiln is the headquarters of the Ardoc family, part fortress and part factory, located in the Bis district of Kaer Maga. Important trials and policy discussions happen in the Judgment Seat, a great hall on the top floor. The Kiln is large enough to house the entire family, if needed in times of trouble. Most of the building contains workshops for the Ardocs to produce their constructs and conduct magical research.⁠
211015176:
Shuryo Onsen

The Shuryo Onsen is a hunting lodge located between the cities of Enganoka and Sakakabe, serving as a retreat for samurai and lords from the surrounding regions. The onsen is surrounded by a wooden palisade and built in the traditional Minkai style. In 4711 AR, Sikutsu Sennaka, the governor of Enganoka, visited the onsen where he was ambushed by a faction supporting Amatatsu Ameiko as the legitimate empress of Minkai and he was defeated in battle.⁠
214442386:
Niishan

Niishan is a small town southwest of Lake Starfall in the nation of Degasi. It is known for celebrating the weeklong Festival of Fire holiday for millennia in honor of the town's founding and prosperity.⁠
215826526:
Pex

The pirate town of Pex is located on the Devil's Arches island of the Shackles, at the south end of the perilous Straits of Balthus. It is a rough, ramshackle settlement, ruled by the capricious Hardluck Massey. He is known for his impulsive punishments against the unfortunates who have annoyed him. Pex boasts a large three-story inn called Damned If It Didn't Rain run by Hegmar of Frembrudd that gathers buccaneers of Ulfen descent as well as Varisian merchants who own warehouses in the town.⁠

227016746:
Ralthorn Manor

Ralthorn Manor was once the summer home of a minor Cassomiri noble family in the Meratt County region of the Tandak Prefecture. Now, it is little more than ruins. House Ralthorn was one of Taldor's many minor noble houses; they had made their money in shipbuilding in Cassomir and spared little expense in building their lavish summer estate in the more bucolic Meratt County. Around 20 years after the estate's completion, it was struck by one of the region's rare earthquakes, which collapsed most of the manor.⁠

It was over a month before anyone came to investigate, and those who did discovered all of the family had been crushed to death in their beds. Although the family's remains were excavated and removed for proper burial, rumours persist that the family still haunts the site. Hunters who venture near the manor report ghostly child-like figures that play amongst the remains of the orchard, watched by a stern woman who seems to manifest from the remains of crushed stone.⁠

258141576:
Slither Cove

Once a reasonably prosperous village, Slither Cove is now nothing but a sinking ruin being rapidly consumed by the surrounding swamp. Slither Cove's current name comes from the wide variety of snakes, lizards, and other reptiles that now inhabit it.⁠
259231786:
Pinnacle

The Pinnacle is the tallest tower in Kaer Maga. In the past, it served as a watchtower, and for decades the city's most influential citizens have fought to control it. A group of aristocrats met and decided it would be best if the tower became a neutral venue where the elite could gather to conduct business without mingling with the rest of the city's rabble. Since then, merchants have met on the lower floors, while the elite teleport to the upper levels to carry out the city's most important business within.⁠
265334956:
Damaq Palace

The Damaq Palace lives up to its name, for this ostentatious structure rivals many palaces of Inner Sea kings, its facade frequently redecorated simply because House Damaq tires of seeing the same thing everyday. The amount of wealth possessed by the Absalom's noble family is simply incalculable to the common plebeian mind,⁠ and although the decoration has remained static for decades, some saying it is in mourning for Aroden and others that it is a sign that the family's wealth is drying up, Scion Lord Kerkis pays no attention to these unfounded rumors.⁠
271245786:
Akafuto

Akafuto, Minkai's second-largest port, is located at the mouth of the Tagiryu River and serves as a major part of the Tian Xia lumber trade. Akafuto exports a wide variety of raw and finished goods, and the city's junks are among the most common Minkaian ships in foreign ports, particularly Tianjing.⁠

Akafuto's most famous temple is the Ukuashi-Ji, dedicated to the god of prosperity Kofusachi, who is said to bless the harvested goods and crafts that flow through Akafuto's markets. Akafuto is also home to the Juhimeiyo School, a monastic institution attended primarily by young nobles looking to work within the imperial court.⁠

Akafuto has maintained a remarkable political stability over the centuries. It has been ruled by a member of the Moniwa family for over a millennia.⁠
282781426:
Barterfall

Barterfall is a neighborhood in the Precipice Quarter, named for its economy and precarious living conditions. It's one of the least dangerous parts of the district, though that's not saying much. Its inhabitants are the descendants of those who were either too poor to move or wanted by the law, and many don't even have jobs, earning their living by fishing, trapping for vermin, and farming whatever they can. Violence and disease are common, and the mansions converted into apartments are falling apart. While its residents want to move to other districts, they also resent the rest of the city for abandoning them. There's an enclave of Kalistocrats who trade coin for what the residents scavenge from the ruins, making them the object of envy and hatred from the inhabitants who barely see them behind their walls and clean houses.⁠
299217566:
Niswan

The port city of Niswan is the capital of the Impossible Kingdom of Jalmeray. Niswan is a many-tiered city of pagodas renowned for its beauty. Every building supports colourful silk banners that flutter in the cold ocean winds, and red stone streets crisscross the hillsides. Cosmopolitan Niswan is a meeting place for travellers and scholars from all over Golarion, and offers sights seen nowhere else in the region. Here, gold-draped eunuchs walk the streets, and Vudran princes offering strange tribute to statues of gods utterly unknown in this region. Niswan is renowned as a centre of religious learning: its High-Holy district is home to scholars and gurus renowned as some of the wisest people on the face of Golarion,⁠⁠ and the city is dotted with numerous shrines, statues, and temples dedicated to the hundreds of deities of the Vudran pantheon.⁠
314327436:
Ushumgal

Ushumgal is a wealthy city on the Alavah Peninsula of Qadira.⁠
315603446:
Posandi Bros.

Posandi Bros. is a very successful masonry business in Breachill, Isger located on the eastern bank of Breach Creek⁠ providing bricks for the town's new buildings. Quentino Posandi is of the fifth generation of his family to own the business.⁠ Most of the employees are related to the family, either by birth or marriage. Day-to-day operations are managed by Amera Lang, and although it is a closely guarded secret, much of the business's success comes from advice given by devils summoned by the family.⁠

Tuskhead Stoneworking has been rivals with Posandi Bros. for a decade and is their main competitor.⁠
328049526:
Erages

Erages is a small fishing community located on the shore of Lake Encarthan in the elven nation of Kyonin. Erages' population is almost entirely aiuvarins who live in virtual exile from the rest of the country.⁠
329333916:
Skala Foothills

The Skala Foothills, in the southern part of the Irriseni province of Wintercrux lie in the shadow of the Kodar Mountains and are rich in resources. More than two dozen mining camps provide Irrisen with tin, copper, iron and gold. Moreover rock quarries produce limestone and granite. According to some mining experts, gems may well be found in the future. A large network of shipping trails cross the Skala Foothills connecting the mining camps to Hope Lost and the town of Zlatomesto.⁠

Many sasquatch families inhabit the wooded areas of the Skala Foothills. Also brutish giants, known as ved, launch small raids against the mining camps and quarries.⁠
331056506:
Mount Onik

Mount Onik is the 10th-tallest peak of the Five Kings Range at 14,714 feet.⁠ It is one of four mountains surrounding the city of Taggoret, alongside Mount Soryu to its west, Mount Langley to its north, and Mount Carissa to its south.⁠⁠
335093716:
Cave of Tiandra

The Cave of Tiandra was the cave complex where Tiandra hid the Azlanti relics she pillaged in the later years of the Age of Darkness. Generations later, Arustun discovered and miraculously interpreted these relics, which enabled the rise of the first human civilization after Earthfall: the Jistka Imperium.⁠

Most Jistkan scholars agree that the legendary Cave of Tiandra is located northeast of what is now Manaket on the Inner Sea coast of Rahadoum. The cave appears to be nothing more than a hillside grotto with a single barren chamber and its low ceiling eroded. However, a narrow pitch in the back of the entrance cavern reveals that beneath the initial level lies a vast network of tunnels, dens, and hollows, with soaring drops and huge domes.

The presence of cullitox has led the scholars to believe that the Cave of Tiandra once had a link to the Plane of Earth, and perhaps to other planes. This might explain how Arustun gained the miraculous insight from the relics found there in -4160 AR.⁠
338773686:
Tolguth

Like the Realm of the Mammoth Lords' largest settlement, Icestair, Tolguth is nestled against the icy walls of the Crown of the World. Unlike Icestair it is a warm, almost tropical town, surrounded by great ferns, rhododendrons, and green cycads. The reason for this vast difference in temperature is the volcanic vents and thermal springs that dot the area. Within this valley roam fantastic creatures that are not found anywhere else in Avistan. These include duck-billed dinosaurs, swift raptors, mighty tyrannosaurs and predatory terror birds like the axe beak. Unsurprisingly, the city is walled for the protection of its inhabitants, but these walls provide only a slight hindrance to the largest of the valley's creatures. Despite being surrounded by a dinosaur-infested wilderness, the biggest danger to the people of Tolguth comes from the Worldwound and its fell demonic influence.⁠

Outcast Fishery

The Outcast Fishery is a series of warehouses and dry docks supporting Magnimar's fishing industry. Members of the guild also have access to an on-site tavern, the Left-Handed Lobster. About one-third of Magnimar's navy uses the facilities here. The fishers have a rivalry with the local merchant vessels, but seem to have lost the attention of their primary patron, House Valdemar.⁠
363023836:
Ngozu

The picturesque port of Ngozu sits on the long cove that gave Mgange Cove island its name.

Ngozu is home to a sizeable fleet of pirate vessels crewed by sailors of Mwangi heritage, nearly all of Bonuwat descent. Residents of the town are loyal devotees of the ancient Mwangi faith of juju, a religion committed to congress with the spirit world of wendo. Ajuoga Baas is the chief wendifa and ruler of the settlement.

Ngozu tolerates non-Mwangi ships, but Ngozu's rules are strict for non-natives, and most laws involve "blood price" punishments.⁠
365359586:
Dongun Hold

The dwarven Sky Citadel of Dongun Hold, located in the Mana Wastes of southeastern Garund, is part of the magic-bereft Grand Duchy of Alkenstar. While the nation as a whole has a primarily human population, Dongun Hold is almost exclusively inhabited by dwarves.

The ancient forge within Dongun Hold is surrounded by gargantuan dwarven statues, seemingly gazing at the forge within. A flaming inverted hammer is engraved into the handle of every item forged in Dongun Hold to show its provenance.⁠
366270446:
El-Fatar

A Pathfinder discovered an enormous set of catacombs beneath a ruined city of Ancient Osirion, in northern Katapesh. Adventurers came to the ruined city to explore the ancient tunnels and over time the small town of El-Fatar sprang up amidst the ruins. The intriguing artifacts discovered attracted many researchers and historians as well.⁠⁠⁠

Skrata

Skrata is a small town on the Rimeflow River, in the westernmost Irriseni province called the Verge that acts as a waystation of goods shipped to the capital of Whitethrone from the north, through the Iceflow River, and as a supply depot for the army. Skrata's docks are always busy, and its warehouses are full with goods destined for the army or the Rimeflow route.⁠
435373976:
Taggoret

The city of Taggoret was the center of the Everlasting Kingdom of Taggoret: one of the five dwarven kingdoms in the Five Kings Mountains, founded in 1562 AR by Taggrick I.⁠

Nowadays Taggoret is a thriving city with iron gates and stone walls on the surface and refined great caverns within the mountain. It is located at the north end of the long trail of dwarven tunnels that run beneath the Five Kings Mountains. Its main industry is iron mining and smelting. Taggoret's iron is known as the finest in Druma and Andoran.⁠
438919246:
Moonwing's Bough

Moonwing's Bough is a small pocket of oak trees in the evergreen Grungir Forest which hosts an ancient shrine to Desna built thousands of years ago, during the reign of the Thassilonian Empire. The shrine is one of the most sacred sites of Desna's faith but very few worshipers attempt to visit it, traveling through the dangerous Grungir Forest. Moonwing's Bough is named after the first priest of Desna who reached the shrine in the modern age. The shrine is preserved in very good condition.⁠

The Ravounel Consulate is the embassy of the free nation of Ravounel, established in 4717 AR by Ambassador Vita Aulamaxa to promote relations and represent its interests in a city as important as Absalom. She promotes the arts, being a lover of theater, and several artists from Kintargo, such as Shensen, have traveled to the city to participate in plays which the Cheliax embassy has taken as insults to its sovereign.⁠
461163056:
Pickled Ear

The Pickled Ear is a bar in the north of the Isgeri town of Breachill frequented by both locals and adventurers, which often leads to fights between the two groups after a few beers. The bartender, Roxie Denn, dislikes these fights, as they drive away new customers from the bar, so she looks for new ways to promote her tavern.⁠

A trapdoor in the bar's basement connects to Citadel Altaerein through a tunnel magically created many years ago, and few in the bar know of its existence.⁠

Jhaltero Estate, located in The Greens district of Kintargo, Ravounel, is the home of House Jhaltero.⁠⁠ It resembles a large and opulent hunting lodge.⁠

Green Ridge

Green Ridge also contains many small farms a result of past sieges. In contrast to much of Absalom, the district tends to be peaceful and quiet.⁠

The Black Grave Tower is a pagoda located in the remote Wild Peaks region of the south-western reaches of the Kelsang Mountains in Zi Ha. Oxjaw Falls

The Oxjaw Falls is a 40-foot-tall cataract formed by the Crook River east of the Slave Trenches of Hakotep, near the headwaters of the river. The Crook drops suddenly from the highlands into the lower reaches of the Brazen Frontier region of Osirion. Oxjaw Falls create a moist and verdant pocket within a rocky grotto. The lizardfolk that live at the base of the cataract worship and guard an ancient altar set into the grotto's mossy walls. At the top of the cataract the water flows through deep channels between flat rocks (resembling the ox's teeth) that allow a slippery crossing for travelers on foot. It is the only safe foot crossing west of the Shallows of Ipeq and has the advantage of being away from the Ipeq guards and gossipy fisher folk.⁠

Dubrov

Dubrov is a small village on the western edge of the Estrovian Forest in Mendev.⁠ During the Mendevian Crusades, its main industry was supplying the holy warriors with arrows, bows, and bowstrings. Legends claim that Dubrov was founded by a pair of half-brothers who shared a common human mother: one was a dromaar, while the other was an aiuvarin.⁠

Bernai Silver Company

Bernai Silver Company is an artisan silverworks and exporter of silver ore located in the Yolubilis Harbor district of Kintargo, Ravounel.⁠ As of 4724 AR, it is led by Davlu Bernai.⁠

Kyzuv

Kyzuv is the de facto capital of the Erutaki nation of Yumyzyl. Located at the mouth of the Moraghiin River, Kyzuv's central location makes it the site of the annual gathering of Yumyzyl clans, which multiplies its normally small population fivefold.⁠⁠
620447236:
Qatada Nessudidia

The Qatada Nessudidia is the largest temple to Asmodeus in Westcrown, and one of the largest buildings east of the Arodennama. Located in Rego Sacero, it stretches four stories tall and is capped with a red crystal skylight roof over its altar that glows with such sinister light that it is difficult to miss at night.⁠⁠
627225146:
Hesperix Manor

Hesperix Manor is an estate on the border of the Umbral Basin and was the residence of the Chelaxian diplomat Perevill Hesperix, but it fell into disuse after his death during the Chelaxian Civil War. Architecturally, the manor harks back to the Chelaxian styles before the Thrune Ascendancy: geometrically symmetric and grey. A few decades ago, Celefin of Pangolais, an agent of the Umbral Court, purchased the manor and it has served as her home ever since.⁠

A follower of the Belevais Doctrine, which precludes undead from following Zon-Kuthon's faith, Celefin of Pangolais retired from government service after realizing she could not advance. She has spent her retirement writing manuscripts on how to eliminate the undead, which has put her on the radar of certain members of the Umbral Court who would like to see her punished for her insolence.⁠
628157796:
Fangwood Keep

Fangwood Keep is a fortress near the Nirmathas–Molthune border in the Marideth River valley. Ownership of the fortress has alternated between the two nations since the beginning of the Nirmathi war of independence. It was built on top of the ancient tower of an elven wizard.⁠⁠
628996896:
Palace Mortales

In the southern deserts of the country of Katapesh, a giant, curving ribcage of a beast rises from the sand. Over the years, travelers have used the giant ribcage as shelter. Sometimes they refer to it as Palace Mortales.⁠

Father's Forge

The Father's Forge is a temple dedicated to Torag in Westgate, whose modest size might cause confusion given that it is the predominant faith of the city's sizable dwarven minority. High Priest Roglund Tergurast explains that every forge and hearth in the city is a shrine to Torag, and the walls display the metal busts of all the priests who have tended the temple for millennia, revealing the quality of its excellent metalwork.⁠

Citadel of the Supreme Elect

The Citadel of the Supreme Elect is a walled complex that houses the offices and residence of the Supreme Elect, who is the chief executive of the democratic nation of Andoran, and who also serves as the mayor of its capital city, Almas. The small keep stands near the western end of the Field of Concord in the Liberty District of Almas. The citadel is topped by a large copper dome, and guarded by a battalion of Steel Falcons. The House of the Demarchy Assembly, which holds the offices of the ministers who advise the Supreme Elect, is also located within its walls, as are buildings that contain the offices of consuls, ministers, and other state officials.⁠⁠
665497346:
Founder's Square

Founder's Square is located in the city center, where the Temple of Calistria and the Laughing Gale are situated. It is the largest public square in the city and therefore the site of the city's festivals.⁠

Tomb of the Iron Medusa

The Tomb of the Iron Medusa is the underground final resting place of House Adella, a noble house of Taldor that once was among the empire's most wealthy and extravagant houses. They descended into diabolism and depravity, and the house was dissolved within the span of a single generation during the 43rd century AR.⁠
678605896:
Obari Imports

Obari Imports is located in the center of Mainmast, offering goods from all over the world. Its owner, Sanjeet Ralama Pakhesh, comes from Jalmeray and has connections with Absalom, Katapesh, Nex, Vudra, and even Tian Xia. Custom orders can be placed for a fee, and he is always protected by his Vudrani monk bodyguards.⁠

Three-Legged Devil

The Three-Legged Devil is a dance hall located in the Jarvis End district of Kintargo. Dance halls in Kintargo combine the functions of a musical venue, tavern, and brothel. The Three-Legged Devil is neither the largest nor busiest such dance hall, but it is Kintargo's oldest, and also notable for the its bardic owner Giveni Henge, who previously allowed it to be used as a safe haven for rebels and fugitives.⁠⁠
690317666:
Nightmoss Camp

As of 4710 AR, a plant called nightmoss that grows in towering cypress trees throughout the Embeth Forest was in high demand. A small number of Uringen residents use their secret formulae to brew the moss into powerful potions that strengthen the body and heal physical conditions. A human druid named Erinin Thulgath stole the secret of nightmoss's healing properties and fled to establish Nightmoss Camp at the southeastern edge of the forest, where Thulgath and her group brew potent alchemical products.⁠
691826636:
Wreck of the Impdrake

The Wreck of the Impdrake is located near the corals of Lady's Cape, having been the site where a crew of Chelish merchants wrecked their ship on the coast when their captain, Linus Halfclasper, mistook the Lady's Light for one of the lighthouses of Magnimar. Those who managed to swim ashore were killed by the boggards of the region over the next two days.⁠
694964686:
Whitethrone

Home to the Jadwiga ("children of the witch-mother"), the descendants of the witch Baba Yaga, Whitethrone was a playground for evil nobles under the 100-year reign of previous Queen Elvanna's family. This has changed since the ascent of Elvanna's successor, Queen Anastasia, in 4713 AR.⁠
697541506:
Ulizmila's Cottage

Ulizmila's Cottage is located somewhere in the Darkmoon Wood, but the locals prefer not to know its location, for those who seek it never return. It is said that Ulizmila, a daughter of Baba Yaga, resides in the cottage, and while legends tell of wonders offered to those who visit, these tales invariably end in tragedy, where the price to pay for her services proves too high.⁠
697554186:
Herne's Oak

Herne's Oak is a barrow deep within the Estrovian Forest of Mendev and the final resting place of the ill-fated hunter Herne Vilhaur. It is guarded by his descendants that were transformed by the curse of the winterthorn: the herne.⁠
705235976:
Sea Wrack Chapel

The Sea Wrack Chapel is a small temple dedicated to Gozreh that serves the pirate city of Port Peril.

Like many seaside settlements, Port Peril has a small shrine dedicated to Gozreh for pious sailors to make offerings to the Lord of Waves. No larger or more impressive than the shrine of a typical fishing village, Sea Wrack Chapel is made from driftwood and discarded fishing nets but is still large enough to provide shelter to those seeking Gozreh's guidance.

Sea Wrack Chapel is tended to by Father Ignalus, a halfling priest who accepts Gozreh worshippers of any creed, including in the form of Shimye-Magalla, a dualistic deity worshipped in the Mwangi Expanse. Father Ignalus is also a meticulous record keeper and has kept track of every single shipwreck that has occurred in the vicinity of Port Peril.⁠
708318616:
Varook's Deep

Varook's Deep is both the lowest dwarf-inhabited point of the Five Kings Mountains at 17,621 feet below sea level, a defensive city that keeps watch over the Darklands, and a trading post that hosts caligni, drathnelars, and underground fey. Its garrison is led by General Flinda Strikespark.⁠

Due to the city's depth, few surface-dwelling dwarves visit Varook's Deep.⁠
709542476:
Fort Riverwatch

Fort Riverwatch is a small town located ten miles northwest of the village of Thornkeep, on the banks of the West Sellen River. It is the last settlement of the River Kingdoms before one crosses into Numeria or Ustalav.

The town serves the barge traffic along the West Sellen. After Mosswater's destruction, Fort Riverwatch is the only port along the river between Lockridge, more than 100 miles to the south, and the muddy fishing town of Dravod Knock, 250 miles to the north. The knights of Iomedae established a garrison at Riverwatch in 4623 AR, and assumed the task of protecting the area. The knights govern the settlement and keep the river and roads safe for travel although they don't have the strength to clean out the lawless village of Thornkeep.⁠
721375316:
Martel

The city of Martel is in the Grand Duchy of Alkenstar, along the Ustradi River west of Alkenstar City and east of the Gunworks. Its most notable features are the two enormous buildings that make up most of the city, which are connected by a number of stone and metal bridges. The Grand Duchy of Alkenstar maintains an extensive treasury in Martel, composed of vaults below the city that are guarded by both clockwork and explosive traps.⁠

The Grand Duchy's gunmarshals make their headquarters in Martel. Additionally, the town is the center of banking for the Grand Duchy of Alkenstar, where the financial practices are as advanced as Alkenstar's level of technology. While this makes Alkenstar effective in their financial dealings, it has left the city-state with a slightly-less-than-trusted reputation throughout the Inner Sea region.⁠
735796246:
Pezzack

Pezzack is a town in western Cheliax on the Sallow Coast of the Arcadian Ocean. Nestled in Devil's Perch among the Menador Mountains, the isolated town has long been a seedbed for sedition against the infernal government far way in Egorian. The crown has responded with several naval blockades and year-long sieges that have left the settlement quite isolated from the rest of the country,⁠⁠ and moved the seat of the Archduchy of Hellcoast from Pezzack to Belde.⁠
739362846:
Crissali's Fine Tomes

Crissali's Fine Tomes, located in Jarvis End of Kintargo in Ravounel, is one of the city's many flourishing bookshops. Crissali's is particularly renowned for both its collection of rare books and magic items,⁠⁠ including a collection of minor magical scrolls and even a more powerful scroll of teleportation.⁠ It is also unusual that the shop's owner, Nandy Crissali, is noticeably apolitical in a city brimming with rebellion.⁠⁠
745005876:
Torrentmoot

Torrentmoot was a camp established on a flat hill so that dignitaries from various nations and factions could observe Belkzen's orc culture and potentially forge diplomatic paths. The initiative was spearheaded by Ardax after Tar-Baphon's forces attempted to subdue the orcs once again. The camp's name derives from its proximity to a vantage point for observing the Flood Road when it inundates annually.⁠

During the flood of 4725 AR, the region's necromantic energies surged, unleashing a horde of undead and those gathered at the camp were forced to evacuate.⁠
748566006:
Goatshead

Goatshead is the main settlement on the Firegrass Isle in the Shackles. It was founded In 4642 AR by a trio of pirate captains who settled on the island. The Pirate Council laid the blame for all and any pirate misbehavior against Sargavan vessels on the Firegrass island buccaneers. Made the scapegoats of every Sargavan complaint, these three captains named their settlement Goatshead and adopted a flag with a white goat's head on a black field.⁠
754754696:
Tuskhead Stoneworking

Tuskhead Stoneworking is a relatively new business located in the heart of the Isgeri town of Breachill on the banks of Breach Creek that specializes in the construction of roads and public structures made of stone. Its owner, Rorsk Axebane, enjoys good relations with the town council but has recently been poaching clients from his competitors at Posandi Bros., suspecting that they are not entirely honorable.⁠
759231386:
Starspine Manor

Starspine Manor is a magnificent residence that would dwarf the surrounding houses were it not for its beautiful gardens. Lord Synarr Daidalos owns the manor, which appeared overnight between two adjacent residences, though this is only a rumor. The spellcaster has purchased the property and uses it for his lavish galas.⁠ He has promised that every seventeenth of Erastus he will hold a gala more magnificent than the last, inviting the city's nobles to attend.⁠
759860796:
Iqaliat

Iqaliat is a small village of Erutaki humans in the Crown of the World, built into the side of Alasek Ridge on the southern boundary of the High Ice some miles west of the Path of Aganhei.⁠ It is constructed beneath the cliff's overhanging ridge. Most of the town is made up of small stone and clay brick buildings and subsists on water from an underground stream.⁠

Iqaliat is protected by its location beneath the cliffs. Travelers can only enter the village through a gatehouse above several earthen ramps. Other sites in the village include low towers inhabited by the village's chieftain Nalvanaq and its shaman Tunuak, Hearthmistress Sonavut's small house, a goat pen, a kennel for the village's dogs, and a subterranean cistern. A small tunnel leads up to the cliff top, where one can find several inukshuks, altars to the Erutaki wind spirits.⁠

The white dragon Vegsundvaag keeps her lair not far from Iqaliat.⁠
766707366:
Volfast's Tower

High in Volfast's Tower stands the undead Volfast Raven-Banner, cursed to forever remain at his post after he drunkenly boasted to Queen Sascha that, if not for his limited mortal life, he would eternally hold back the Frozen Fog itself in the queen's name. Unfortunately for him, she granted his request, and transformed him into his current state. Here he remains until someone can defeat him in single combat. Some say that whoever defeats him would not only free him, but also inherit his cursed post, while others say they would gain a great, hidden wealth somewhere in the tower.⁠
796135886:
Matten Cleave

Matten Cleave is a town in the Swardlands of the Isle of Kortos used primarily by local farmers for transporting crops to the port of Kerrick and buying agricultural supplies.⁠ It is located near the northwestern shore of the Isle of Kortos on the Inner Sea, northeast of Kerrick.⁠
799009526:
Sublime Square

The Sublime Square is one of the best open-air markets around, boasting an excellent variety and unparalleled quality, selling everything from fine clothing and magical items to delicious ingredients and unmatched weapons. The stalls are run by Kalistocrats who have obtained permits from the city; those of lower rank have to settle for simply setting up a cloth to sell their wares. Blackjackets patrol the square all day, but since crime is very low in Kerse, there are few problems here.⁠
800913366:
Babschu-Jong

Babschu-Jong is a major city in the samsaran country of Zi Ha on the continent of Tian Xia. It is located on a southern peak in the Kelsang Mountains and is a major trade connection on the route between Linvarre's capital of New Oppara and Zi Ha's nominal capital of Sangpo-Jong. Primary trade materials include artwork, gems, herbs, incense, livestock, and stone from Zi Ha, which are traded for grain, iron, and textiles.⁠
806099246:
Halidon

Halidon is a small logging community on the edge of the northern Backar Forest in Molthune. Lying roughly halfway between the capital of Canorate and Braganza, the town is a frequent stop for travelers and has, therefore, a large number of inns with respect to its resident population.⁠⁠
815832266:
Scallion's Wrap

Scallion's Wrap is a village in Nirmathas whose only reputation lies in the way they prepare for Winter Week. Many decades ago, a pack of wolves carried off the village's sheep and destroyed the crops in the weeks leading up to Winter Week. It was then that a witch, using her cauldron and a magic rock, created stews for the entire village. Since then, the preparation of this event has fallen to the witch's descendants, currently the halfling Kupyn Baro.⁠
825936996:
Arsmeril

The cliff-side elven village of Arsmeril can be found where the northwestern Mierani Forest meets the Steaming Sea. Along with the settlement of Crying Leaf, it is the only elven settlement in Varisia,⁠⁠ and like its companion on the far side of the Mierani, it is an outpost of the elven nation of Kyonin who wish to keep a closer eye on the ruins of Celwynvian.⁠
837868686:
Sphinx Head

The Sphinx Head or Black Sphinx is the largest sphinx statue in Osirion, located in the desert between Shiman-Sekh and the Junira River. It is constructed from black granite, and has sunk up to its chin in the desert sands.⁠ Its features are believed to be those of the Sky Pharaoh, Menedes I, staring into the center of Osirion.⁠
837959636:
Wetan

Wetan was a lirgeni city that was swallowed by the waters when the Eye of Abendego opened. A tribe of athamaru found the ruins in the Abendego Gulf and claimed them as their territory. They began to disrupt the city's magical defenses until they reached an observatory with copper plates bearing strange symbols. When they activated the arc within it, fiendish energies lashed out at them. The once peaceful tribe roams the region, attacking anyone who approaches, and the malevolent energies continue to spread throughout the waters of the gulf.⁠
839760426:
Mirnura

Mirnura was once the capital of Jistka Imperium, founded by the legendary hero Arustun. The city was named after Arustun's beloved wife. It was situated on what is now the northern coast of Rahadoum, on the Fallen Peninsula north of the Path of Salt.

Mirnura was the main target in Ancient Osirion's campaign to destroy the Jistkan empire. When Osirians burned the city to the ground, they used millions of tons of salt to eradicate all signs of life around it. The Path of Salt region was named for this epic razing.

Powerful sandstorms sometimes reveal hints of monuments, and the vaults of Jistkan emperors are thought to show themselves to individuals of royal Jistkan descent. One of these vaults, known among the treasure hunters as the Halite Crypt, lies in tremendous depths and is rumored to still be protected by a Jistkan behemoth golem by the name Helatoros.⁠
842311276:
Canorate

Canorate is the capital of the nation of Molthune. It is an impressive city which manages to combine architectural splendor with defensive fortifications. It is said that even the poor of Canorate live in luxury, and to a certain extent this is true—citizens allow a select number of necessary laborers to live in fine accommodation (but naturally kept separate from the rest of the population) in order to encourage them to settle in the city.

The city's most exclusive district is known as the Sweet Orchard. Non-residents are not allowed to enter this exclusive section without a valid work or travel permit.

The Imperial Castle dominates the center of the city. The ruler of Molthune, Imperial Governor Markwin Teldas, maintains an impressive war room within the castle. Pride of place is given to a large scale model of the Inner Sea region, on which the generals plot their next campaigns.⁠
846320466:
The Conservatory

The Conservatory is a secret, Jalmeri training school for spies located on the inaccessible island of Grand Sarret in the Obari Ocean.

Housed in a collection of buildings that once served to house the harem of the legendary Maharajah Khiben-Sald, the Conservatory trains students in the arts of seduction, cooking, music, and the careful manipulation and influence of governments around the world.⁠ Once they complete their training, the graduates are sent to courts, noble houses, and seats of power throughout the Inner Sea region in order to further the ambitions and interests of the government of Jalmeray. They report back to the Conservatory on a regular basis, where their information is catalogued in an extensive, ever-growing library on the island, one of the greatest repositories of secret knowledge throughout the Inner Sea region.⁠
902743316:
Satyr Shoals

The Satyr Shoals are a group of islands in the southern part of Iblydos formed by sand and shells being carried up from the Obari Ocean. The unstable nature of the islands means permanent settlements are frequently buried or resurfaced as the topology of the islands change. Because of this, none of the nearby city-states want the land, and anyone found here are likely pirates or other types who want to stay away from the eyes of any authorities.⁠
921548106:
Songbird Preserve

The Songbird Preserve is located in the Three Sisters and is a collection of parks with flora and fauna cared for by the druid Jaxira Daralamir. She is likely the only priestess of Shelyn in this pirate city and seeks to bring natural beauty to it.⁠
922628146:
Zandrek's Pesh Palace

Zandrek's Pesh Palace is a famous pesh parlor in the city of Katapesh. It is a round, domed building surrounded by bronze columns. Its massive copper door is a sculpted face of a laughing man. There are no other doors in the interior but only silk and bead curtains. Multiple private chambers line the first ring of the building while a second ring is filled with statuary, cushions, couches, and wandering minstrels and dancing girls. The center of the structure is a lovely courthouse filled with plants, marble flagstones and a central pool full of colorful fish. Zandrek's Pesh Palace is the most popular den of iniquity in a city full of sin and vice. Master Zandrek cares to satisfy all of his customers' desires. A small army of exotic slaves are especially trained to see to the needs of Master Zandrek's guests.⁠
935323856:
Nyshire

Nyshire is a small town in the Archduchy of the Heartlands between the capital of Egorian and Halmyris.⁠
972468456:
Rickety bridge

An old rickety bridge spans the Thorn River about a dozen miles south of the Thorn River bandit camp.⁠ The river is about 20-foot-deep here, passing between two rugged hills. Local bandits are aware that the creaking bridge will surely collapse if they do not cross it one by one.⁠
973084976:
Lekshey

Lekshey is a city of the arts, music, and entertainment in the nation of Zi Ha. The nation's largest communities of bards, entertainers, and musicians live in Lekshey, and the city stages monthly music festivals that each encompass a genre of music.⁠
977804636:
Galduria

Galduria is a town in central Varisia, located on the western shore of Ember Lake. Generally thought of as a dependent of the city-state of Magnimar, most of the town's wealth is generated by the trade of grain and lumber across the lake and along the Lampblack River. Its true claim to fame is its arcane college, the Twilight Academy, the founding of which in 4629 AR by Galdurin Barmier was the establishment of the town.⁠ The Twilight Academy rivals the larger colleges in Varisia, the Stone of the Seers in Magnimar, and Korvosa's Acadamae. The college was founded specifically to avoid the political pressure and intrigues of those two cities. The Twilight Academy has a reputation for undertaking many experimental and unconventional practices. Nevertheless, locals turn the other way regarding its strange ways in exchange for the money that the college is able to provide for various civic projects.⁠⁠
980917846:
Orochel House

The Orochel House is a mansion that serves as an inn for visitors to the city of Pangolais. The government of Nidal prefers to keep outsiders concentrated in one place unless they demonstrate devotion to the Midnight Lord. The establishment is exquisitely decorated, the service is excellent, and the prices are affordable. The only problem is the constant surveillance that the Umbral Court maintains over the place.⁠
990866916:
Bastardhall

The ruined fortress of Bastardhall, originally called Arudora Manor or Castle Arudora, is located on Lake Laroba near the West Sellen River on the eastern border of the Ustalavic county of Varno.⁠⁠

Bastardhall is best known in Ustalav for the black coach that leaves it once a century in search of seven people descended from the Arudora family, which are brought back to Bastardhall for unknown purposes. The internal workings of Bastardhall are obscured from the outside world: the castle is perpetually shrouded in fog, and attempts to magically probe its interior reveal a veil of powerful holy magic warding the interior of the castle's island. The only contact the castle makes with the rest of the world occurs once a century, when the fog parts to let the black coach pass.⁠
997697496:
Roshik

Roshik is a town in Almhult⁠ located on the southern Steaming Sea coast of Cape Almhult, between Asre to the west and Helsingbyen to the east.⁠
1006034866:
Aroden's Redoubt

Aroden's Redoubt is a ruined fort that was the first line of defense against a possible invasion from Garund. It is located above the Arch of Aroden on the far south-west of Corentyn before the entrance to the city. The fort is collapsing under its own weight, as is the bridge on which it stands, and historical tours no longer visit it.⁠

Aroden's Redoubt is one of the nine famous forts of Corentyn, the City of Nine Forts, according to the classical listing.⁠
1009134546:
Ungkore

The Iblydan city of Ungkore is the capital city of the city-state of Pol-Ungkore. The city, along with the surrounding territory of Pol-Ungkore, has experienced a number of cycles of economic booms and busts. For Ungkore itself, each boom led to widespread building projects, leading to a state today where the city is built upon multiple previous layers, rising up to 300 feet above the area around it. These undercities are a perfect environment for crime to thrive beyond the levels Ungkore can manage.⁠
1018458436:
Steam Pit

The Steam Pit is a massive sinkhole located in the Linnorm Kingdom of Icemark. Nearly 500 feet in diameter, the pit emits foul-smelling steam and hot air, and is believed by the Varki to be cursed.⁠
1020461886:
Kantaria

The Chelaxian town of Kantaria stands just west of the Sedna River, between the Barrowood and the Menador Mountains to the north.⁠ It is the capital of the Archduchy of Menador.⁠
1022800776:
Ukhrul

Ukhrul is one of the numerous prosperous cities of the Wide Water region of the Impossible Kingdoms of Vudra. Ukhrul sits at the eastern end of the Seabound Road, which with its completion heralded a new era of prosperity for the once desolate region of the Western Ghats. Ukhrul itself, however, sits on the eastern side of the Johar Mountains in the north-west of the Wide Waters region, sited nearby the source of the Matra River.⁠

Ukhrul has a reputation as a somewhat grim city, ruled by the militaristic Rajah Shavit, and is renowned for its production of firearms and other technological weapons. Rajah Shavit offers these weapons for export but only to distant mahajanapadas so that his expansionist ambitions cannot be hampered by the advanced weapons made in Ukhrul being used against him by his neighbours.⁠
1026602526:
Lord-Mayor's Menagerie

The Lord-Mayor's Menagerie is a public park located in the Capital District district of Magnimar. The park's unusual name stems from the collection of bizarre taxidermy and living creatures on display. Canayven Heidmarch and Sheila Heidmarch, a pair of local Pathfinders who run the Heidmarch Manor Lodge, use the park as a place to display their unique menagerie. This strange collection includes an eyeless, and therefore relatively harmless, basilisk, a tame 14-foot-tall ape named "Prince Mandali", and the egg of a tarn linnorm.⁠
1051218596:
Aerie Club

The Aerie Club is an establishment where Kerse's elite go to enjoy the best amenities, including trainers and a fitness center, a sauna, and a bar where they can mingle with other influential members of society. The building dates back to the city's beginnings, and although its owner isn't a Kalistocrat, its clientele certainly is. Only after dozens of visits is a client granted VIP status, giving them access to even more magnificent facilities.⁠

Tamran

Holy Xatramba

The ruins of Holy Xatramba (sometimes also spelled Xatremba) lie in the eastern jungle of the Mwangi Expanse, southwest of the city of Kibwe.⁠

The city was founded in 3699 AR, at the site of Volnagur's first defeat (which happened in 909 AR).⁠⁠ Its religion was an unique mix of ancestor worship and worship of Pharasma and its memory is revered by the Mwangi people.
1072665436:
Drowning Stones

The ruins of the city of Drowning Stones, located in the northern Mwangi Jungle of the Mwangi Expanse, were abandoned by its population when it began to sink into the swamp. It sits about halfway between the Olongo River to the north and the Vanji River to the south.⁠ Today, only the central fortress remains relatively dry.⁠ The city takes its name from the massive standing stones that served as pillars for the central forum.⁠
1073642836:
Clear Waters

The city of Clear Waters floats atop Lake Clear Waters in the centre of the Forest of the Sacred Eye and draws visitors from across Xopatl and beyond. Clear Waters is renowned for its beauty and anyone wishing to travel through the city must use one of the city's small boats, most of which are decorated with a special flower that blooms every new moon. Clear Waters draws in the most visitors during the full moon, however, as during the height of the full moon Lake Clear Waters begins to glow with moonlight.⁠
1079307336:
Karpad

Karpad is a small village approximately 100 miles north of Nidal's capital, Pangolais, just south of the region known as the Atteran Ranches. It has been ruled for centuries by the Barons of the House of Boroi.⁠
1082504046:
Harborhorn

The Harborhorn is the home of Port Peril's harbormaster, who is responsible for inspecting every ship that docks at the pirate port. It is located on its own small island just off the larger island of Crescent Harbor.

As of 4712 AR, Harborhorn was the home of the notoriously stern dwarven harbormaster Tsojmin Kreidoros. Little goes on within the bustling city that escapes the harbormaster's notice.⁠
1090478266:
Kuratown

Kuratown is a small town in Numeria populated largely by orcs.⁠
1092771796:
Hekastor

Hekastor was a city and golemworks of the Jistka Imperium known to be active ca. -3600 AR. It was destroyed and buried by earthquakes of divine nature millennia ago. Golems still roam the site, and its former residents slowly evolved into morlocks who remain active in the area.⁠⁠ These Jistkan morlocks obsessively work to power 17 glowing magical pylons out of fear of releasing a destructive threat. The morlocks have been unable to power the pylons by any means other than the sacrifice of arcane magic spellcasters beneath the pillars.⁠
1106581946:
Solitary Pool

The Solitary Pool is a small oasis and caravanserai in the Meraz Desert of Qadira. It is operated by Razinia, who appears to visitors disguised as a jann but is secretly a ghul.⁠
1129824146:
Grayce

Grayce is an Ustalavic settlement in the south-west of the county of Caliphas with the border of Lastwall, the Path River, a mere stone's throw away.⁠ This proximity means the town is a bridge to Lastwall with the Chapel Bridge, a drawbridge that can span the Path, literally fulfilling this role. From the southern end of the bridge, roads lead to Vigil, north-west of Grayce, and to Vellumis to the south.⁠

The townsfolk are predominantly farmers, shepherds, and weavers.⁠
1136574936:
Peijia

Peijia is the largely empty capital of the Tian Xia nation of Bachuan, built on the northern shore of Naikang Bay. Established by the country's founder Grandfather Pei, the city was designed to hold up to 200,000 inhabitants. However, as of 7211 IC barely 50,000 people had followed Grandfather Pei's commands and relocated there, leaving much of the city uninhabited.⁠

As of 7224 IC, many of the city's buildings are overrun with monsters, magical plants, and squatters despite a recent influx of investment in the city.⁠
1140404596:
Feasting Hall of Cayden Cailean

In Mivon of the River Kingdoms, an unusual hill devoid of vegetation has a ring of standing stones on its summit. At irregular intervals these stones transform into a feasting hall from which comes music and laughter, and those who enter on these occasions can join in the revelry. Some say that this is the Feasting Hall of Cayden Cailean, the god of ale and wine.

In the morning, the standing stones replace the hall once more, although the hillside reeks of ale and wine. As of 4710 AR, the last occurrence was also marked by the presence of a large quantity of blood among the stones.⁠
1160136936:
Ghivel's Townhouse

Ghivel's Townhouse is located in Rego Corna and was the home of a family devoted to Abadar who suffered greatly during the chaos of 4710 AR. The townhouse contained statues and paintings of their god, as well as a basement where they hid things they did not want others to see.⁠
1169860536:
Elesomare

Elesomare is a small farming and lumber-producing colony, established in pre-revolutionary times by the then province of Andoran on the far-away shores of Arcadia.⁠ As it was overwhelmingly settled by commoners looking for a better life abroad, it greeted Andoran's radical change in government with great hope and sympathy. Being separated from the motherland and the many political and economic compromises that a large government necessitates, the citizens of Elesomare are more idealistic than their counterparts in Avistan. In recent years, the colonists have been attempting to decrease the local influence of the authoritarian and sometimes brutal Lumber Consortium. Although the government in Almas does not support this subtle insurrection, they have been noticeably slow in responding to the Consortium's call for help and reinforcements.⁠
1197795856:
Eranmas

The walled city of Eranmas is on the shores of Lake Encarthan. It is the second largest city in Molthune, and home of the country's navy. This navy is the largest fleet on the lake, and its main role is to blockade Tamran, capital of the "rebel" nation of Nirmathas. The city is governed by Lord Resket.⁠
1206816566:
Stormhollow

Stormhollow, formerly known as Lorra's Hollow, was a village located in the Umbral Basin that was destroyed by velstracs during a shadowstorm. The village was founded by halflings who escaped the empire of Cheliax and sought a more fulfilling life. Those hopes were shattered by the velstrac attack, which transformed the inhabitants into greater shadows that now roam the village. Their houses are now filled with spikes and nails, and the flora has vanished from the streets.⁠
1232358726:
Mount Yogan

Mount Yogan is a volcano in southern Minkai along the Kyojin Mountains, near the source of the Sakehiyaku River. It is one of the Three Fires, along with Mount Kumijinja in the Kamifushi Mountains and Mount Kazunan in the central Kyojin Mountains.⁠
1251334886:
Concerned Residents' Union

The Concerned Residents' Union is Eastgate's second council, unrecognized as official. However, because the district is such a close-knit community, decisions made by the residents are often final, while official recognition is merely a formality. Their headquarters are located in a red brick building in the district center, and landowners and shopkeepers coordinate their schedules to meet regularly. The union's operations could be considered organized crime, as they decide who to elect as Nomarch, which lieutenants to be promoted to the Post Guard, and what favors the council owes to the union's businesses.⁠

The organization operates through donations to charitable causes, though this money tends to disappear as it passes through various channels, and any criminal investigation is terminated before it even begins, simply by one resident whispering something to another until the guard catches on. The union isn't interested in lining its own pockets; it aims to maintain the calm and supportive atmosphere of Eastgate, even if it means marginalizing some people. The two cults, the Children of Spring and the Circle of Stones, are a concern, as President Gelda Dellby's son, Rance, has joined the Children as a recruiter. This betrayal has hardened her heart, and she seeks to close the park and eliminate the cults. The more sons and daughters who join the cults, the more likely her proposals are to be approved.⁠
1252217286:
Pillar Wall

Stretching across multiple districts of Korvosa, Pillar Wall is one of three colossal pieces of ancient Thassilonian architecture that have come to define the skyline of the city. Stretching across Citadel Hill, what remains of the ancient Pillar Wall is a hundred feet high and forms the border of three districts: The Heights, Gray, and South Shore. At its western end, stands the almost equally impressive Gatefoot.⁠
1256158586:
Castle Corvischior

Castle Corvischior (once known as Korsinoria Palace) is a seemingly abandoned fortress near the village of Corvischior in the eastern Ustalavic province of Varno. Situated near Lake Korsinoria, it was once the county seat of Varno's ruling family, House Tiriac. The count is believed to have abandoned his home long ago to go gallivanting abroad, ignoring the needs of his people. In his absence, rumors of hauntings have begun to be told about his home: people see strange lights at night, or see gates open to admit unmarked carriages.⁠⁠ The truth behind these rumors, is that the castle is still inhabited by a Tiriac: the enigmatic Counte Risotmaur. Unbeknownst to most of his citizens, he has lived there for over two centuries using a variety of guises, as he is, in fact, a vampire.⁠

The Old Forest Tower is one of the aeon towers that Aroden placed around the Isle of Kortos.⁠ The tower is a 300-foot-tall mudbrick step pyramid with a flat 10-foot-wide top and four uneven tiers.⁠⁠

The tower is located in the Swardlands on the Isle of Kortos in the Immenwood.⁠

Unlike the other Aeon Towers, this tower contains a shrine to Aroden inside.⁠

The entrance to the tunnel is a cave mouth at the bottom of Lake Rogshagrox which leads to a vertical cavern over 4 miles in length. The heat at the bottom of the Dragon's Gullet is unbearable.⁠
1281804106:
Soduras

Soduras is a small fishing community on the Iceflow River, which forms the border between the Irrisen province of Bleakmarch and the Linnorm Kingdom of Hagreach. Due to its location, it is frequently used as a stopover and resupply point for raiding parties of ice trolls, witchwargs, or mercenary bands conducting cross-border raids.⁠

As of 4713 AR, the town's ruler Baroness Vjera encourages the martial visitors and orders the townsfolk to provide housing, food, and entertainment to them. Soduras' north end houses a large number of inns, as well as fighting pits that cater to ice trolls and witchwargs. Human mercenary companies usually stay in the south end of the town and enjoy themselves at the brothels of Madame Plana Vectenstyn. Life is hard for Soduras' residents, but these hardships have also inspired tough adventurers.⁠

Tenna's

  • Upslope House; and

1408590526:
Dunholme

Dunholme is a ruined settlement in Taldor's Verduran Forest.⁠ The site fell victim to a mysterious event known as "the Dunholme Doom" in which an as-yet-unknown threat emerged from a well, first claiming the lives of townsfolk Verniya Klamer, Maix Vivermer, and Jasmique Tunhold.⁠ A trade road still runs through Dunholme toward Belhaim and Wispil further north.⁠
1415082286:
Kazuhn City

Kazuhn City serves as the capital of the Kazuhn Prefecture in the heart of Taldor, but all is not well in Kazuhn City. Almost three quarters of the city stands empty: half having been abandoned, and another quarter ravaged by the great fire of 4702 AR. Most of what remains are industrial buildings devoted to keeping the agricultural produce of Kazuhn Prefecture endlessly flowing to the distant capital of Oppara.⁠

The regions of Kazuhn City abandoned by polite society, now known as Squatter City, are far from truly empty. A shadow economy now nestles amongst the ruins of Kazuhn. This economy revolves around drugs and other illegal produce, particularly flayleaf, and even the best efforts of the city guard, led by Almoril Tersian, have failed to root out this corruption. The nobility often talk of finally demolishing the abandoned regions of the city but the expense has thus far prevented them from doing this. So, Squatter City remains a home to criminals, the destitute, and the monsters and vermin that prey on both.⁠

The Brotherhood of Silence moved to this location in 4725 AR and have begun to influence the region; the Lion Blades are monitoring their activities.⁠
1426238576:
Wisher's Well

Wisher's Well is one of the lesser known Thassilonian ruins in the greater Sandpoint area. This circular stone tower is 30 feet high, and the interior drops away into a 100-foot-deep shaft, ending in an underwater cavern connected to Sog's Bay.⁠⁠

This submerged complex was formerly the laboratory of Mazmiranna, who later abandoned it when she became the fifth runelord of greed. It has since been taken over by the albino alghollthu master Vorimorath, who has been drawn to Wisher's Well by the promise of Thassilonian treasures and the alghollthu master has restored Mazmiranna's wards and guardians. Myriad monsters also dwell in the complex, including Vorimorath's ulat-kini and faceless stalker minions, the latter of which have been modified to be able to breathe water.⁠

New Stetven

The city of New Stetven is located on the southern banks of Lake Reykal (also known as Needle Lake) in central Brevoy and serves as the nation's capital. The city has been the seat of power in Brevoy since the warlord Choral the Conqueror founded it over the ruins of the Taldan settlement of Stetven⁠ in 4499 AR after uniting the separate nations of Issia and Rostland under his rule.⁠⁠

New Stetven is a bustling trade city that acts as a hub for exporting Brevoy's rich supplies of grain, fish, timber, and ore to the rest of the northern kingdoms, such as Mendev and Numeria, and down the East Sellen River to the River Kingdoms. Food from Rostland sustains many of the northern realms, where constant bandit raids or invading demonic armies make farming difficult. In exchange for these much-needed goods, imports of exotic items from all corners of Avistan and beyond, such as rare Numerian skymetals and ancient Osiriani relics, are common in New Stetven's rough-and-tumble marketplaces.⁠

The city, which has made prodigious use of wood in constructing everything from mansions, to streets, to forts, is also known as "The City of Wooden Palaces." Due to the prodigious number of wooden structures within its walls, the city boasts several volunteer fire brigades that protect its buildings—citizens join these brigades mostly out of a sense of civic pride. There are but two notable stone structures in New Stetven: the Ruby Fortress, which houses the Dragonscale Throne sits, and the Bulwark of Gorum, a temple to the Lord of Iron.⁠

Snow and slush cause the streets to turn to mud for most of the year.⁠

1480552396:
Urfa-Halij

Urfa-Halij is an ancient memorial located in the Sophra Prefecture and is sacred to both the people of Taldor and their neighbouring rivals in Qadira. Urfa-Halij marks the location of the first ever battle between the people of Taldor and, as it was at the time, the Empire of Kelesh. Known as the Battle of Urfa to the Taldans and the Battle of Halij to the Qadirans, Urfa-Halij recognises both perspectives and stands as a testament of respect for those soldiers lost by both sides of the war. Both sides recognise this place as sacred and, by custom, no sort of conflict takes place for miles around the monument. This has made it one of the most peaceful and fertile areas along the war-ravaged border between Taldor and Qadira, with rabbits being particularly common.⁠

The Urfa-Halij monument itself consists of two raised arms, one wielding a Taldan-styled longsword, the other a Qadiran scimitar, the blades of both meeting in the middle where a huge diamond is set. This diamond catches even the dimmest of light, making it seem as if the blades are sparking even on a moonlit night. Many debate, due to the striking nature of Urfa-Halij, if it is really a monument to the dead or if, in fact, it is secretly a tribute to the glory of war.⁠
1482476276:
Narona

Unlike the inhabitants of the nearby city of Pezzack, Narona's residents never returned after the settlement's destruction.⁠
1495755596:
Bank of Absalom

The Bank of Absalom has a far-reaching power, influencing trade and finance beyond the City at the Centre of the World across the Inner Sea region. From the Bank of Absalom, its bankers can influence the flow of trade and commerce by adjusting interest rates, approving (or not) massive loans, and issuing debt collection orders. The Bank of Absalom is nominally a secular institution, rather than a temple devoted to Abadar, the god of trade, but, in reality, the Bank of Absalom is run by Vroclaw of Brevoy, the most powerful Archbanker of Abadar in Absalom. The Bank of Absalom takes its religious orders from the Vault of Abadar in the Ivy District, but Vroclaw controls all loans and debt collection. Vroclaw's critics accuse him of facilitating the exploitation of indigenous peoples to extract profit, a claim Vroclaw does not deign to refute.⁠⁠

Kublan Grove

The Kublan Grove is no clump of woodland but a tangled mass of rafters, scaffolds, and masonry that serves as a testament to the flighty whims of the Taldan aristocracy. Located in Taldor's Lingian Prefecture, the Kublan Grove began life as a construction project that started soon after the prefecture's rise in popularity. Approximately twenty years ago, three Opparan baronets, all cousins from House Kublan, borrowed against their family's ancestral lands, buying up several miles of farmland to construct a grand retreat for the nobility. In their lust to provide every possible luxury, the project's scope increased massively, bloating from an original plan for a simple manor house to, eventually, being an entire community devoted to vice and hedonism, but it was not to be.⁠

Funding dried up and construction halted. Now the half-finished buildings lie abandoned amidst a forest of scaffolding, empty save for a few wild animals and a community of squatters. House Kublan occasionally hires bands of thugs to sweep through the grove and chase off the squatters, desperately hoping to attract new investors as the Lingian Prefecture's popularity grows.⁠

Temple Row

Temple Row is a neighborhood teeming with temples to various deities, most of them related to the sea and weather, located in The Docks. 1598859476:
Erithiel's Hall

Erithiel's Hall is a serpentine earthen mound located in the western Fierani Forest of Kyonin. Several stories in height, between 20 feet to 100 feet across and several miles in length, the mound is said to predate the elves and is rumoured to be connected to the fey of the First World. According to the most popular myth, Erithiel's Hall is named for an ancient fey hero, Erithiel, who in the dawn of history fought against the earth serpent Garukresh. Their epic battle is said to have left deserts and seas in its wake before Garukresh was finally slain where he now lies at Erithiel's Hall. The victorious Erithiel supposedly then built a vast barrow-palace within the remains of his defeated foe. Those few elves who have tried to excavate Erithiel's Hall have found themselves plagued with bad luck and earning the hatred of the region's fey creatures.⁠

Sable Sands

Sanctum's Watch

Sanctum's Watch was built to guard a pass in the Southern Range of the World's Edge Mountains in the Taldan province of Ligos, a purpose which it no longer serves. Sanctum's Watch is a fortress expertly hidden amongst the mountains and the valley itself was a sight of much bloodshed in the early days of the Grand Campaign, when the Taldan army faced off against the forces of Qadira. Seen as an easy way to march an army into the soft belly of Taldor, the valley was eventually fortified, which discouraged Qadira from ever trying this approach again and led to disuse. Morcei

Morcei was a quiet hamlet in the east of the Ustalavic county of Lozeri, situated under the south-eastern branches of the vast Shudderwood; the Mothburn has its source nearby.⁠ Recently the peacefulness of the hamlet was shattered when local lumberjacks felled a tree near to the settlement known as the 'Daemon Hand'. From inside the Daemon Hand flew swarms of bats, or 'flying wolves' as the locals now call them. The bats made their home in the belfry of the local Pharasmin church house from where they terrorize the locals. The church bell tolls inexplicably each morning, summoning the bats home, and the locals fear some mighty winged lord is controlling them.⁠⁠

Drenchport

The city of Drenchport is on Tempest Cay in the Shackles. Its proximity to the dreaded Eye of Abendego means the city is constantly lashed by storms. The city itself is constructed from driftwood and the remains of wrecked ships.

Drenchport's most infamous tavern is the Drowned Dwarf. It serves surprisingly tasty black kelp beer, but is notorious for its very high murder rate.⁠

The ruler of Drenchport is the pirate lord known as the Master of the Gales.⁠

The city is the home of the gnome salvager Tho Rimplethember, who is well known as an expert on the currents and winds of the dangerous Eye of Abendego.⁠

1782194396:
Tastikka

Tastikka is a small village of the strix Kitkasiticka tribe in the Ravounel Forest. They traditionally isolated themselves from human contact until the defeat of the Grundlescorn sisters encouraged them to pursue careful and cautious negotiations. The tribe's rokoa Rarrnir, who came to power after the abdication of her predecessor Solmestria, had met with representatives from the Silver Council as of 4719 AR but as of that time had yet to secure an agreement concerning the new settlements along the Ravounel Forest's borders.⁠⁠
1787136546:
Bleachbone Cave

Bleachbone Cave is a concealed cavern located in the Vergan Forest in Razmiran. This cave remains shrouded in secrecy, its sole entrance artfully hidden by an enormous, bone-shaped white rock. Few outside of its clandestine inhabitants are even aware of its existence, rendering it an ideal refuge for those seeking to elude the ever-watchful eye of the Razmiri clergy.⁠

In recent times, a small group from Whispertruth, a faction dedicated to opposing the rule of the Living God Razmir, has sought sanctuary within Bleachbone Cave. Korellen Duinsol, an aiuvarin ranger, leads this band of rebels. Concerned about Razmir's apparent knowledge of their activities and the countermeasures he has been taking, the group has chosen to keep their newfound sanctuary a closely guarded secret.⁠

Unbeknownst to the rebels and their captive, a malevolent presence known only as the Ancient One resides in the deepest recesses of the cave, patiently waiting. It comes from the Dominion of the Black and patiently waits for the right living mortal to possess in order to escape its trap in this cave.⁠

Lions' Square

After every war, famine, and political conflict, the district receives new migrants, and with the prohibition of faith in Sarenrae by Stavian I, many of the inhabitants are devout followers of the goddess. After the War for the Crown, many nobles, exiled or dissatisfied with the new direction of the country, have come to enjoy the freedom that Absalom offers.⁠

1845547346:

Tangled vines climb its walls and overgrown thickets and brambles cover the surroundings, but the castle has not deteriorated such as an ancient site should have. Each month on the night of the new moon, its great iron-horned clock tower rings. Rumors persist that something lurks within, and the rumors are supported by sightings of swiftly moving shadows and strange lights flickering from the castle's lonely towers.⁠⁠

1912325526:
Daggermark

The largest city in all of the River Kingdoms, Daggermark has maintained enough political and economic stability to secure an abundant supply of food, a rarity in the chaotic Broken Lands region of northeastern Avistan. Daggermark is so stable that it even has a thriving industry and is wealthy enough to mint its own currency.⁠⁠

The main reason for this stability are the two guilds for which the city is so famous: the Daggermark Assassins' Guild and the Daggermark Poisoners' Guild. These two organizations often work hand in hand, as the assassins favor the use of poisons, believing that only amateurs leave behind an obvious cause of death. Few bandit lords would be stupid enough to attack Daggermark for fear of being found poisoned, strangled, or having succumbed to some other seemingly "accidental" death.⁠⁠

At the peak of Maidenspool's growth, Bradesmar openly boasted that the Master of the Gales's city would soon be just so much driftwood. These merfolk are willing to help sailors by granting them boons and even helping them repair their ships. Once every seven years, the merfolk of Crescent Cove choose a "sea-groom" from amongst the Obari pirates and a "land-bride" from amongst the residents of Holomog's coastal provinces, though, despite the names, either can be of any gender. These simulacra seek to bring prey to the Famished Mind to consume, allowing it to grow in knowledge and subtlety and spread its enigmatic agenda.⁠

The city is also famous for its high priest Razdara who leads her acolytes on pilgrimages into the Outer Sphere. Her most recent trip saw her return alone, looking deeply haunted and carrying predictions of some dire fate that she claims is soon to befall the people of Wide Water.⁠

Beast

The Beast is the largest crane in the world. It is located at edge of the Long Pier, near the center of the Docks district of Absalom. The Beast is used to unload the heaviest and largest loads in Absalom. It is a five-story stone windmill-like massive structure, with a long wooden winch-and-rope system sticking out of the top. The entire building can rotate on its axis and its main arm can extend out from its normal 25-foot length. Built 500 years ago, it is well maintained, capable of lifting nearly 60 tons to a height of 55 feet. When lifting loads no more than 10 tons, it can swing them in a 360-degree arc anywhere within 100 feet of its central tower. Its structure contains 16 human-operated treadwheels. All the warehouses built around the Beast are multi-storey buildings with central shafts to allow the Beast's cables to raise and lower cargo to any of their floors.⁠

Responsible for the operation of the Beast is the First Harbormaster. Running the Beast requires engineering expertise, thus the crane is hired out to a professional crane master.⁠ Recently, Adrielle Neprathep of House Fyrlenn was replaced by Amaziah Meneha as the chief engineer of the Beast.⁠

In 4499 AR, during the Red Siege, the Beast defended itself, using a one-ton block of stone as an oversized flail.⁠
